story.title: Houthis Gain Control of Strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Threatening Oil Exports
story.summary: Iran-aligned Houthi rebels have captured Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical shipping lane at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. This takeover follows the withdrawal of Yemeni government forces and poses a significant threat to Saudi oil exports. In response to recent drone attacks, Saudi Arabia has halted oil transfers through a major pipeline as a precautionary measure.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of developments from July 22-27, 2026—military threats, congressional war-powers action, shipping and oil-market pressure, Houthi claims, and ceasefire diplomacy—not the conflict’s full origins, all operations, or its eventual outcome.

explore_lenses.label: What changed on the ground at Bab el-Mandeb?
explore_lenses.title: A rapid Houthi advance reached the strait
explore_lenses.summary: Houthi forces took Mayyun/Perim after Yemeni government troops withdrew, following the capture of Mokha and reported advances along the nearby coast. That gives the group a position on Yemen’s side of the chokepoint, but it does not by itself establish uncontested control over all navigation through the international strait.

claims.text: A Yemeni government official and eyewitnesses told Euronews that Houthi fighters reached Mayyun (Perim) after government forces withdrew; the island divides the narrowest section of Bab el-Mandeb into two shipping lanes.
AP reported that a senior official in Yemen’s internationally recognized government and a Houthi official both confirmed the island’s capture.
Houthi political-bureau member Hazem al-Assad said shipping and trade would remain safe; Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree subsequently said Saudi ships were an exception to that assurance.

explore_lenses.label: How did the confrontation escalate this quickly?
explore_lenses.title: The offensive followed wider Saudi-Houthi escalation
explore_lenses.summary: The takeover emerged amid renewed fighting in Yemen and cross-border attacks on Saudi targets, rather than as an isolated maritime event. UN officials have described the escalation as a risk to civilians, infrastructure and freedom of navigation.

claims.text: According to Euronews, the Houthis captured Mokha on September 10 and then moved onto Mayyun/Perim as part of a rapid offensive against Saudi-backed government forces.

The UN said on September 8 that more than 5,600 households had been displaced across Taiz and southern Al Hudaydah since fighting escalated on September 3, and it condemned Houthi cross-border attacks affecting civilians and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry, in its first reported statement after the Houthi entry into Mokha, called for Saudi Arabia to end its blockade of Yemen and for negotiations to resume; Saudi Arabia says it retains the right to take measures necessary to protect its security and facilities.

explore_lenses.summary: Saudi Arabia has paused the East-West pipeline while inspecting it after drone attacks, and says it is giving Iraq time to act against launches from its territory. International maritime authorities are urging risk assessments, but no verified arrangement reopening or securing Bab el-Mandeb has been announced.

claims.text: Saudi Arabia’s Energy Ministry said the East-West pipeline was shut as a precaution after multiple September 10 drone attacks in the Riyadh and Medina regions; emergency and technical teams were assigned to secure the line and verify its integrity.

Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry said it would not respond at this stage after Iraq’s prime minister asked for time to prevent attacks from Iraqi territory, while reserving its right to protect its sovereignty, people and facilities.
The IMO says it is monitoring Red Sea incidents under UN Security Council reporting requirements and has urged shipowners and operators to assess risks before transiting the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

story_report.summary: Houthi fighters have captured Yemen’s Mayyun, also known as Perim Island, after government forces withdrew, giving them a position at the narrowest part of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The island divides that passage into two shipping lanes, raising concerns for Saudi oil exports and commercial traffic through the Red Sea gateway. Saudi Arabia separately halted transfers through its East-West pipeline as a precaution after drone attacks on September 10, while assigning emergency and technical teams to inspect and secure the line.

sections.heading: Offensive Displaces Thousands in Yemen
sections.body: According to Euronews, the island seizure followed the Houthi capture of Mokha on September 10 during a rapid offensive against Saudi-backed government forces. The United Nations said more than 5,600 households had been displaced across Taiz and southern Al Hudaydah since fighting escalated on September 3. The UN also condemned Houthi cross-border attacks affecting civilians and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

sections.heading: Houthis Offer Conditional Shipping Assurance
sections.body: A Yemeni government official and eyewitnesses told Euronews that Houthi forces reached Mayyun after government troops withdrew; AP reported that officials from both the internationally recognized government and the Houthis confirmed the capture. Houthi political-bureau member Hazem al-Assad said shipping and trade would remain safe, but military spokesman Yahya Saree later said Saudi vessels were excluded from that assurance. Iran called for Saudi Arabia to end its Yemen blockade and resume negotiations, while Saudi Arabia said it retains the right to protect its security and facilities.

sections.heading: Maritime Operators Assess Red Sea Risks
sections.body: The International Maritime Organization says it is monitoring Red Sea incidents under UN Security Council reporting requirements and has urged shipowners and operators to assess risks before transiting the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Caroline Rose of the Soufan Center told Euronews that some operators may instead route vessels around the Cape of Good Hope, a shift she said could add weeks and increase insurance, personnel and other costs.

unresolved.text: The disposition of forces on nearby Hanish islands and the Houthis’ ability to enforce restrictions on passing vessels remain unclear.
Publicly available evidence does not establish the full chain of command behind the Houthi offensive or whether external actors directly directed it.
Saudi Arabia has not provided a verified timetable for restoring the East-West pipeline, and no confirmed counter-operation or negotiated maritime-access arrangement has been identified.

related_stories.title: Saudi Arabia Closes Key Oil Pipeline Following Drone Attack from Iraq
related_stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has shut down a vital oil pipeline after it was targeted by drones launched from Iraq. This closure is expected to impact oil flow and exacerbate the ongoing energy crisis in the region. In response to the incident, Iraq has initiated investigations into the drone attack, which originated from an area near the Iranian border.

related_stories.title: Saudi Arabia Shuts Key Pipeline Following Drone Attacks
related_stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has shut down its East–West pipeline after multiple drone attacks from Iraq set the pipeline on fire. This pipeline is vital for transporting oil to the Red Sea, circumventing the Strait of Hormuz, and the incident is expected to impact oil and fuel prices significantly.

related_stories.title: North Korea Launches Ballistic Missiles Following Joint Military Drills
related_stories.summary: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles into the sea, according to reports from Seoul. This action occurred a day after the conclusion of joint maritime drills involving the United States, South Korea, and Japan, which North Korea had deemed provocative.

related_stories.title: Trump Expresses Support for a Unified Ireland During Visit
related_stories.summary: During his visit to Ireland, President Donald Trump stated that he would 'love' to see Ireland reunified, calling it 'fantastic' and 'inevitable.' His comments were made while attending the Irish Open golf tournament and meeting with Irish leaders, including Micheál Martin. Trump suggested that reunification could happen soon, despite Downing Street's commitment to the Good Friday Agreement.
